label: Bansal S04: opioid with paralytic ileus
title: Ongoing opioid with paralytic ileus
statement: Persistent prescription of opioid analgesics to a patient with paralytic ileus [62, 63]

source.document: Bansal N, et al. Development of prescribing indicators related to opioid-related harm in patients with chronic pain in primary care. BMC Med 2024;22:5, Tables 3-4
source.citation: Bansal N, Campbell SM, Lin C-Y, Ashcroft DM, Chen L-C. Development of prescribing indicators related to opioid-related harm in patients with chronic pain in primary care - a modified e-Delphi study. BMC Med 2024;22:5. doi:10.1186/s12916-023-03213-x

plain_summary: Opioids slow the bowel. In a person with paralytic ileus, where the bowel has stopped moving, they can make it worse.

medicine_groups.name: Opioid pain medicines
medicine_groups.note: Tablets, capsules, liquids, patches and injections used for pain count. Codeine combined with paracetamol counts, for example Panadeine Forte. Targin is oxycodone with naloxone. Methadone and buprenorphine used for opioid dependence are not counted here. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too. Count only opioid analgesics used for pain in the source population. If the indication is unknown, report at most a possible finding and ask what the product was used for. Exclude substitution treatment and codeine cough preparations. Count Physeptone tablets when used for pain. Do not match Physeptone Liquid as a tablet. Count Opod-D Syrup only when its use for pain is confirmed.

needs_facts.what: Paralytic ileus during this opioid course
needs_facts.meets: A clinician confirmed active ileus during the opioid course. Clinical suspicion alone keeps the finding possible and calls for same-day review. An unknown history needs routine confirmation.

options.words: A clinician confirmed active ileus during the course
A clinician suspected active ileus during the course
No active ileus during the course, including an earlier resolved episode

needs_facts.what: Reason for the opioid course under review
needs_facts.meets: Ask only if the product and record leave its purpose unclear and the other evidence fits. Only chronic non-cancer pain outside palliative care qualifies for this course. An unknown reason leaves the finding possible.

options.words: Chronic non-cancer pain outside palliative care

needs_facts.what: Duration of the opioid course under review
needs_facts.meets: Ask only when repeat prescriptions span at least three calendar months and the dates, quantities and directions leave continuity uncertain. One continuing course of at least three calendar months qualifies. A shorter course or separate courses do not. If unknown, keep the finding possible.

options.words: One continuing course of at least three calendar months
A shorter course or separate courses

rule_for_models: Check people over 18 for more than one Group A opioid prescription for pain in one course of at least three months, using course dates or quantities, directions and supply dates. Exclude cancer pain, palliative use, substitution treatment, cough products, separate short courses and ileus resolved before treatment. For same-day review, cite the opioid supplies, the line recording active ileus and any separate line that gives the reason for pain treatment. If a supply would run out at the directed dose before the next supply, cite the dated line showing treatment continued through the gap, such as a hospital medicines record, before counting them as one course. Clinically suspected active ileus needs same-day review as a possible finding. If the other evidence fits, keep an unknown ileus status, age or reason for this opioid course open for a routine check. If repeat supplies span at least three calendar months but the record leaves the course length unclear, ask whether they formed one continuing course. Keep an unknown answer possible.
cannot_be_seen: Whether the ileus is current, how well the bowel is working, why the opioid was started, and care given by a hospital.
ask_the_gp: A review of whether the opioid is safe to continue and of bowel function.
